mainTopic: Is preventing צער בעלי חיים (animal suffering) a Torah law (דאורייתא)?
overview: This amud asks whether the duty to prevent צער בעלי חיים, animal suffering, comes from the Torah. First the גמרא tries to prove it is דאורייתא from the קל וחומר of loading to unloading, and from רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling about an overloaded animal. Each proof is pushed back. Then the גמרא tries to prove the opposite from the רישא of the משנה, where the passerby is פטור if the owner sits down. That proof is answered: he may only be exempt from helping for free. A סימן then lists five more sources: בהמת, בהמת, אוהב, שונא, רבצן. Proofs come from a גוי's animal, from יין נסך, from a ברייתא about whose animal and whose load, from choosing between a friend and an enemy, and from limiting 'enemy' to a Jewish enemy. Each one is answered by איבה, by saying the case is about loading, by saying a ברייתא follows only רבי יוסי הגלילי, or by the value of overcoming one's יצר הרע. The amud ends as the גמרא begins the last source, רבצן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First proof: both opinions use the קל וחומר based on animal suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that both the רבנן and רבי שמעון agree in principle to the קל וחומר from loading to unloading. The only factor that makes unloading 'stronger' seems to be צער בעלי חיים, so it must be a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what both of them say, we learn that animal suffering is a Torah law. Even רבי שמעון only disagreed because the פסוקים are not clearly marked. If they were, he would also make the קל וחומר. Why would that קל וחומר work? Isn't it because of animal suffering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא. It points to the קל וחומר from loading to unloading that both sides accept in principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר says: if you must help with loading, surely you must help with unloading. For that to work, unloading must have some extra reason behind it. The גמרא suggests that reason is the animal's suffering under its load. Since the קל וחומר is learned from the Torah's verses, צער בעלי חיים would be a Torah-level concern.

keyTerms.meaning: Suffering of living creatures (animals)
From the Torah, a Torah-level law
An 'all the more so' argument, from a lighter case to a stronger one
The verses are clearly identified (we know which verse speaks about which case)
We expound or derive

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not reject the logic of the קל וחומר. He only says we can't use it because we don't know which פסוק refers to loading and which refers to unloading. That is why the גמרא can count him as agreeing in principle.

phrases.english: From the words of both of them we learn
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the רבנן and רבי שמעון from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: that animal suffering is a Torah law.
For even Rabbi Shimon only said his view
because the verses are not clearly identified.
But if the verses were clearly identified,
we would derive the a fortiori argument.
Because of what?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דָּרְשִׁינַן?
phrases.english: Is it not because of animal suffering that we would derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the inquiry by drawing a conclusion from the earlier dispute about loading and unloading.
steps.raayaObject: That צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The קל וחומר from טעינה to פריקה, which both the רבנן and רבי שמעון accept in principle

steps.title: Rejection: maybe the reason is money loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe unloading is 'stronger' because of חסרון כיס (money loss), not because of the animal's suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the reason is money loss. The argument would go like this: if you must help with loading, where there is no money loss, then surely you must help with unloading, where there is money loss!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It offers a different reason why unloading is stronger than loading: money loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only needs some extra factor in unloading. That factor could be money loss, because an overloaded animal might die or its load might be ruined. If so, the קל וחומר proves nothing about צער בעלי חיים.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe (a common word for pushing back on a proof)
Loss of money (literally, 'lack in the pocket')
Loading a burden onto an animal
Unloading a burden off an animal
All the more so

phrases.english: Perhaps it is because there is monetary loss.
And this is what he is saying:
If in the case of loading,
which involves no monetary loss, one is obligated,
then unloading, which does involve monetary loss,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by offering another basis for the קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the possibility that צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קל וחומר could rest on חסרון כיס instead of צער בעלי חיים

steps.title: Challenge: loading can also cause money loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the rejection. Loading can also cost the owner money, since he may miss the market or be robbed while he waits. So money loss cannot be the difference, and the original proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no money loss in loading? Aren't we talking about a case where, while he waits, he misses his chance at the market, or thieves come and take everything he has with him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'money loss' answer. It shows that loading has money loss too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both loading and unloading involve money loss, money loss can't be what makes unloading 'stronger'. The only remaining difference is the animal's suffering under its load. So this challenge puts the first proof back in place.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (a case)
Meanwhile, in the meantime
He misses his market
Thieves

phrases.english: But does loading involve no monetary loss?
Are we not dealing with a case
where in the meantime he misses his market,
or else thieves come
and take everything that he has with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 2, which restores the proof of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that loading has no חסרון כיס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loading also involves money loss (missed market, theft), so money loss can't be the factor that makes unloading stronger.
steps.whatToRemember: Money loss happens in both loading and unloading. So the קל וחומר must rest on צער בעלי חיים, which exists only when the animal is stuck under its load.

steps.title: Second proof begins: רבי יוסי הגלילי on an overloaded animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second proof from the סיפא of the משנה. רבי יוסי הגלילי says you don't have to help an animal carrying more than its proper load.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that animal suffering is a Torah law, because the latter part of the משנה teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, if the animal was carrying more than its proper load, you don't have to help it. The פסוק says 'under its burden', which means a load it is able to carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second proof by quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי. This step sets up the quote, and the actual inference comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads 'its burden' as a normal load the animal can handle. If the owner overloaded it, the מצוה to help does not apply. The גמרא will use this to figure out what the other opinion holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that), a word that introduces a supporting proof
The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
Obligated to attend to it
Its burden, its load

phrases.english: Know that animal suffering is a Torah law,
as the latter clause teaches:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
If there was on it more than its proper load,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. Some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: one need not attend to it,
as it says: "Under its burden,"
meaning a load that it is able to bear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate proof for the same claim.
steps.raayaObject: That צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי הגלילי in the סיפא of the משנה

steps.title: The inference: the תנא קמא requires helping even an overloaded animal
steps.stepSummary: From רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling, the גמרא infers that the תנא קמא requires helping even an overloaded animal. The only reason for that seems to be צער בעלי חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this show that the first תנא holds you must help it? What is his reason? Isn't it because animal suffering is a Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second proof. If רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts you, the תנא קמא must obligate you, and that only makes sense because of the animal's suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner overloaded his animal, he caused the problem himself, so there is little reason to help him for his own sake. If the תנא קמא still obligates helping, the reason must be the animal itself. So צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from this it follows
The first (unnamed) opinion in the משנה
What is the reason?

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the second proof in the גמרא's effort to show that צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law, which matters for how strictly the הלכה treats an animal's pain.

phrases.english: Does this not imply that the first tanna
holds that one must attend to it?
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּצַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא?
phrases.english: Is it not because animal suffering is a Torah law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר זָקוּק לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the quote in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied view of the תנא קמא, who obligates helping even an overloaded animal

steps.title: Maybe They Only Disagree About Reading 'Under Its Burden'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי יוסי הגלילי. The argument may be about how to read the words תחת משאו, not about צער בעלי חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps they disagree about the words 'under its burden.' רבי יוסי reads them to mean a burden the animal can carry. The רבנן do not read anything special into those words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 5. The disagreement between רבי יוסי הגלילי and the תנא קמא may have nothing to do with צער בעלי חיים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed the תנא קמא must help even an overloaded animal only because of צער בעלי חיים. Now the גמרא says the real argument is about reading the פסוק. רבי יוסי learns from תחת משאו that the מצוה covers only a fair load, while the רבנן do not limit the מצוה from those words. So the רבנן's ruling can come straight from the פסוק, and צער בעלי חיים is not needed to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe (opens another way to read things)
They disagree
We interpret (we learn a rule from the exact words of a פסוק)
'Under its burden', words from the פסוק (שמות 23:5)

phrases.english: Perhaps they disagree about the words 'under its burden',
as Rabbi Yosei holds:
we interpret 'under its burden' to mean
a burden that it is able to bear,
and the Rabbis hold:
we do not interpret 'under its burden' that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי יוסי הגלילי. It does not show that צער בעלי חיים is NOT a Torah law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the disagreement had to be about צער בעלי חיים. It could instead be about reading תחת משאו.

steps.title: Proof From the First Case: Animal Suffering Is Not a Torah Law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now argues the other way. If the passerby is פטור when the owner sits down, the animal is still suffering, so צער בעלי חיים must not be a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law. The first part of the משנה teaches: if the owner went and sat down and said, 'Since you have a מצוה to unload, unload,' the passerby is exempt, because the פסוק says 'with him.' If צער בעלי חיים were a Torah law, why would it matter whether the owner helps or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches direction. It now tries to prove that צער בעלי חיים is only דרבנן, using the רישא of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts the passerby when the owner refuses to help, based on the word עמו ('with him'). But the animal suffers just the same whether the owner helps or not. If the Torah cared about the animal's pain, the owner's laziness should not cancel the duty, so the exemption suggests צער בעלי חיים is not from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that (introduces a proof)
The first part of the משנה
'With him', from the פסוק. The owner must work together with the helper
If it would enter your mind (if you thought)
What difference does it make to me?

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. Steps 1–5 tried to prove צער בעלי חיים IS from the Torah. This step tries to prove it is NOT.

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע דְּצַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: Know that animal suffering is not a Torah law,
for it is taught in the first part of the mishna:
if the owner went, sat down, and said to him:
'Since there is a מצוה upon you to unload, unload!'
he is exempt, as it says 'with him.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: And if you think animal suffering is a Torah law,
what difference is it to me if its owner is with him,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לִי כִּי לֵיתֵיהּ לְמָרֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and what difference if its owner is not with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע דְּצַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs that it IS a Torah law were rejected, the גמרא tries a proof for the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the משנה: the passerby is פטור when the owner sits down and does not help (from עמו).

steps.title: Exempt Only From Helping for Free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. פטור may mean only that he does not have to help for free. He still must help for pay, so צער בעלי חיים can still be a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law. Do you think 'exempt' means completely exempt? Maybe he is exempt from helping for free but must help for pay. This is what the Torah means: when the owner helps, work with him for free. When the owner does not help, work for him for pay. And really, צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 7. The word פטור in the משנה may not mean the passerby can walk away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 assumed פטור means no duty at all, which would leave the animal suffering. The גמרא reads it instead as 'exempt from working for free.' The passerby must still unload, but the owner has to pay him. The animal is helped either way, so the proof falls away and צער בעלי חיים can stay a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (keeps the original position)
Do you think...? (questions an assumption)
For free
For pay
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: פטור here may mean 'exempt from helping for free,' not 'exempt completely.' So the proof from the רישא does not work, and the question of צער בעלי חיים stays open.

phrases.english: Actually, animal suffering is a Torah law,
do you think 'exempt' means completely exempt?
Perhaps he is exempt for free, but obligated for pay.
And this is what the Merciful One is saying:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִיתֵיהּ לְמָרֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ – עֲבֵד גַּבֵּיהּ בְּחִנָּם,
phrases.english: when its owner is with him, work with him for free;

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי לֵיתֵיהּ לְמָרֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ – עֲבֵד גַּבֵּיהּ בְּשָׂכָר,
phrases.english: and when its owner is not with him, work for him for pay,
and actually, animal suffering is a Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, מִי סָבְרַתְּ פָּטוּר פָּטוּר לִגְמָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the רישא. It shows the משנה fits with צער בעלי חיים being a Torah law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed פטור means completely exempt. It may only mean exempt from helping for free, with a duty to help for pay.

steps.title: Memory Aid for the Coming Proofs
steps.stepSummary: A סימן (memory aid) lists keywords for the five proofs the גמרא is about to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: 'animal of', 'animal of', 'friend', 'enemy', 'collapser'.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up what comes next. It lists keywords to help you remember the next five proofs, in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סימן does not argue anything. Each word is a hint for one upcoming source in the debate about צער בעלי חיים. As each proof comes up, try to match it to its keyword.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid: a list of keywords for coming sections
A friend
An enemy
An animal that tends to lie down under its load

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: animal of, animal of,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. It's just a memory aid, a list of keywords for the proofs coming up.

phrases.english: friend, enemy, collapser).

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימַן בֶּהֱמַת, בֶּהֱמַת, אוֹהֵב, שׂוֹנֵא, רַבְצָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition line that sets up the next series of proofs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a memory aid listing the five coming proofs.

steps.title: A gentile's animal is treated like a Jew's animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from a ברייתא that צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law. We must unload a גוי's animal just as we would a Jew's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a ברייתא supports רבא: 'A gentile's animal, he tends to it like a Jew's animal.' If animal suffering is a Torah law, that explains why. But if it is not a Torah law, why should he tend to it like a Jew's animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to support the view that צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no obvious reason to help a גוי's animal, since the Torah's מצוה of unloading speaks about your fellow Jew's animal. If we must still help, it seems the reason is the animal's own suffering. That is a Torah-level concern.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this source supports him
He tends to it (helps unload the animal)
The suffering of living creatures (animals)
From the Torah (a Torah law)

phrases.english: Let us say that a ברייתא supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבא, who holds that צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּהֱמַת גּוֹי מִטַּפֵּל בָּהּ כְּבֶהֱמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The animal of a gentile: he tends to it like the animal of a Jew.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא –
phrases.english: Granted, if you say animal suffering is a Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי מִטַּפֵּל בָּהּ כְּבֶהֱמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: that is why he tends to it like a Jew's animal.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: But if you say animal suffering is not a Torah law,
why does he tend to it like a Jew's animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First of the five proofs hinted at by the סימן in step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: בהמת גוי מטפל בה כבהמת ישראל

steps.title: The reason may be avoiding hatred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. We help the גוי's animal because of איבה, not because of the animal's suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because of hatred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא may have a different reason: to avoid creating hatred with the גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי saw Jews helping only Jewish animals, hatred could grow. So the help could be a step מדרבנן to keep peace. That means the ברייתא does not prove that צער בעלי חיים is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Hatred, bad feelings between people
There (in that case)

phrases.english: There, it is because of hatred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling can be explained by איבה instead of צער בעלי חיים.

steps.title: Support from the case of idolatrous wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the איבה answer. If the animal carries יין נסך, one does not have to help it. That fits better if צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also logical, since it was taught: 'If the animal was loaded with יין נסך, he does not have to deal with it.' If animal suffering is not a Torah law, that explains it. But if it is a Torah law, why does he not have to deal with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to back up the answer it just gave, that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal suffers just the same whether it carries wine or anything else. If the Torah cared about the animal's pain, the type of load should not matter. Since the ברייתא lets him skip helping, it seems the reason for helping was never the animal's suffering.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also logical (support for the last answer)
Wine used for pouring to idols
He does not have to deal with it

phrases.english: This is also logical, as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיְתָה טְעוּנָה יֵין נֶסֶךְ – אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ.
phrases.english: If it was loaded with idolatrous wine, he does not have to deal with it.
Granted, if you say it is not a Torah law,
that is why he does not have to deal with it.
But if you say it is a Torah law,
why does he not have to deal with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the דחיה of step 11 (the reason is איבה, and צער בעלי חיים is not דאורייתא).
steps.raayaObject: צער בעלי חיים is not דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: אם היתה טעונה יין נסך אין זקוק לה

steps.title: The wine case is about loading, not unloading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the support. The ברייתא means only that he need not load יין נסך onto the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: to load the animal with idolatrous wine, he does not have to help.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the יין נסך ברייתא so that it says nothing about the animal's suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Loading a load onto an animal does not relieve any pain, so צער בעלי חיים is not involved. The ברייתא only frees him from handling idolatrous wine while loading. Unloading a suffering animal could still be a Torah duty.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (rereading a source)
To load it (put the load on the animal)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: וּלְהַטְעִינָהּ יֵין נֶסֶךְ אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ.
phrases.english: And to load it with idolatrous wine, he does not have to deal with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וּלְהַטְעִינָהּ יֵין נֶסֶךְ אֵין זָקוּק לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The support from the יין נסך ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as speaking about loading, where there is no animal suffering.

steps.title: A gentile's animal carrying a Jew's load: 'you may hold back'
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says that for a גוי's animal with a Jew's load, the rule is וחדלת. This suggests צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'A gentile's animal with a Jew's load: "you shall hold back."' If animal suffering is a Torah law, why say 'you shall hold back'? It should say 'you shall surely release it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, this time to show that צער בעלי חיים is not דאורייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וחדלת in the פסוק means there are cases where you may hold back from helping. The ברייתא applies that word to a גוי's animal. But the animal is suffering, so if the Torah cared about that, the ruling should be עזב תעזב, that you must help.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a new proof)
And you shall hold back (from helping)
You shall surely release (help unload)
It should have said

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A gentile's animal and a Jew's load: "you shall hold back."

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: And if you say animal suffering is a Torah law,
why "you shall hold back"?
It should have said "you shall surely release"!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּהֱמַת גּוֹי וּמַשּׂאוֹי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof in the series, now arguing the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: צער בעלי חיים is not דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: בהמת גוי ומשאוי ישראל וחדלת

steps.title: That ruling is about loading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the view that צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law. It explains that the ברייתא speaks about טעינה, loading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, animal suffering is a Torah law. There, it is about loading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof. The ברייתא is talking about loading, where the animal is not in pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the job is loading, there is no suffering to relieve, so צער בעלי חיים is not involved. That is why one may hold back. The proof falls away, and צער בעלי חיים can still be דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (keeping the original position)
Loading a load onto an animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up טעינה (loading) and פריקה (unloading). צער בעלי חיים only matters in unloading, because then the animal is in pain under its load.

phrases.english: Really, animal suffering is a Torah law,
and there, it is about loading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the first half of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be about loading, where there is no animal suffering.

steps.title: Then why must one help with a Jew's animal and a gentile's load?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the loading answer from the second half of the ברייתא. There, a Jew's animal with a גוי's load gets עזב תעזב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, say the last part: 'A Jew's animal and a gentile's load: "you shall surely release."' If it is about loading, why 'you shall surely release'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15 using the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole ברייתא is about loading, there is no animal suffering anywhere in it. So why must one help in the second case? Something other than the animal's pain must create the duty there, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Say the last part (of the same source)

phrases.english: If so, say the last part:
A Jew's animal and a gentile's load: "you shall surely release."
And if it is about loading, why "you shall surely release"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about loading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In loading there is no animal suffering, so nothing explains the duty to help in the סיפא.

steps.title: Because of the Jewish owner's distress
steps.stepSummary: The duty in the סיפא comes from the suffering of the Jewish owner, who is stuck waiting. It does not come from the animal's pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the distress of the Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in the second case one must help because the Jewish owner is stuck and troubled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal belongs to a Jew. He is held up on the road until it is loaded, so helping him ends his trouble. The loading answer stands, and צער בעלי חיים can still be a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: The distress of the Jew (the owner)

steps.whatToRemember: For now the loading answer holds: in the סיפא you must help only because of the Jewish owner's trouble, not the animal's pain. Step 22 will challenge the idea that this ברייתא is about loading at all.

phrases.english: Because of the distress of the Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason for the ruling (the owner's distress rather than the animal's)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since there is no animal suffering in loading, there should be no duty to help in the סיפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The duty in the סיפא comes from the Jewish owner's distress, so the loading answer stands.

steps.title: Then the first case should also require help
steps.stepSummary: If the Jew's suffering creates a duty in the סיפא, the רישא should also have one, since there too a Jew is involved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even the first case should require it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If a Jew's suffering is enough to require help, the first case should require help too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא the animal belongs to a גוי but the load belongs to a Jew. That Jew also loses out if the load is stuck. So why does the ברייתא say וחדלת, that you may walk away?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
The first part of a ברייתא or משנה
Also; too

phrases.english: If so, even the first clause too!
phrases.notes: In the first clause a Jew owns the load. He should suffer from the delay just as much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the Jewish owner's suffering creates the duty in the סיפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jew is also involved in the רישא, so the same reason should create a duty there too.

steps.title: Who is driving the donkey
steps.stepSummary: In the רישא a גוי drives the animal. In the סיפא a Jew drives it and is stuck waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first case is where a גוי is driving the donkey. The second case is where a Jew is driving it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases differ in who is standing there with the donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suffering that counts belongs to the person stuck on the road with the animal. In the רישא that person is a גוי, so there is no Jew to help. In the סיפא it is a Jew, so you must help.

keyTerms.meaning: A donkey driver
The last part of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: The first clause is about a gentile donkey driver
the latter clause is about a Jewish donkey driver.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא בְּחַמָּר גּוֹי סֵיפָא בְּחַמָּר יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses involve a Jew who suffers, so both should require help.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the סיפא has a Jew standing there waiting, because a Jew is driving.

steps.title: How do we know who is driving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basis there is to assume a Jew's animal has a Jewish driver and a גוי's animal has a גוי driver.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes you so sure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the basis of the answer just given. The ברייתא never mentions drivers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says whose animal it is. The last answer added a detail about the driver. The גמרא wants to know where that detail comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What
You decided for certain

phrases.english: What makes you decide this for certain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why we may assume the animal's owner is also its driver

steps.title: A person usually walks with his own donkey
steps.stepSummary: Usually the owner goes along with his own animal, so a גוי's donkey has a גוי driver and a Jew's donkey has a Jewish driver.
steps.simpleTranslation: Normally, a person walks behind his own donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is describing the normal situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People usually drive their own animals. So when the ברייתא says the animal is a גוי's, it means a גוי is with it. When it says the animal is a Jew's, it means a Jew is with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The usual way things are
A person
His donkey
Goes; walks

phrases.english: The ordinary way of things is
that a person walks behind his own donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְתָמָא דְּמִלְּתָא אִינִישׁ בָּתַר חֲמָרֵיהּ אָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The normal case is that the owner drives his own animal.

steps.title: The verses quoted are about unloading
steps.stepSummary: The verses the ברייתא quotes, וחדלת and עזב תעזב, speak about unloading. So the ברייתא cannot be about loading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the words 'you shall hold back' and 'you shall surely help' are written about unloading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15, that the ברייתא is about loading. The verses the ברייתא quotes are about unloading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 saved the view that צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law by saying the ברייתא speaks about loading. But the ברייתא quotes verses that are written about unloading, so it must be talking about unloading. That brings back the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it that
Unloading a burden from a fallen animal
That are written

phrases.english: But "you shall hold back" and "you shall surely help"
are written about unloading!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״וְחָדַלְתָּ״ וְ״עָזֹב תַּעֲזֹב״ בִּפְרִיקָה הוּא דִּכְתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back and challenges the answer of step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא speaks about loading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses verses about unloading, so it must be about unloading.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really is about unloading. It follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says that preventing an animal's pain is not a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the loading answer and agrees the ברייתא is about unloading. It then says the ברייתא follows only one תנא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does show that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law, but only according to רבי יוסי הגלילי. So it cannot prove the הלכה for everyone. Other תנאים can still hold that it is a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
A תנא who holds that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law
Not from the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about a גוי's animal and a Jew's load is about unloading. It follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, so it does not decide the question for everyone.

phrases.english: He said to him: Whose view is this?
It is רבי יוסי הגלילי,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.
phrases.english: who says: the pain of animals is not a Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 by changing approach
steps.terutzResolutionType: Says which תנא the ברייתא follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about loading, so it fits the view that צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about unloading and follows רבי יוסי הגלילי alone.

steps.title: Helping an enemy load comes before helping a friend unload
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a friend needs help unloading and an enemy needs help loading, you should help the enemy. If animal pain were a Torah law, unloading should come first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If a friend needs help unloading and an enemy needs help loading, the מצוה is to help the enemy, so that you train yourself to overcome your evil inclination. And if you think animal pain is a Torah law, wouldn't helping the friend be better?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to try to prove that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unloading takes away an animal's pain, but loading does not. If that pain were a Torah concern, the friend's unloading should come first. Since the ברייתא puts the enemy's loading first, it seems the animal's pain is not a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; a proof is coming
A friend
An enemy; someone you dislike
To push down his evil inclination
If you would think

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A friend needs help to unload, and an enemy needs help to load –
the מצוה is to help the enemy,
in order to overcome his evil inclination.
And if it enters your mind
that the pain of animals is a Torah law,
wouldn't that one be better for him?
phrases.notes: 'That one' means unloading the friend's animal, which stops the animal's pain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אוֹהֵב לִפְרוֹק וְשׂוֹנֵא לִטְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third source hinted at by the סימן in step 9 (אוהב), a new attempt to show צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.raayaObject: That צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that puts the enemy's loading before the friend's unloading

steps.title: Fighting your evil inclination still comes first
steps.stepSummary: Even if צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law, the Torah values overcoming your evil inclination more, so helping the enemy comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, overcoming his evil inclination is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא's ruling fits even if animal pain is a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say the animal's pain doesn't matter. It says that breaking your bad feelings toward an enemy is even more important. So the ברייתא proves nothing about whether צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Better; takes priority

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא teaches that working on your own character can outweigh removing an animal's pain, even when both are Torah duties.

phrases.english: Even so,
overcoming his evil inclination is better.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, כְּדֵי לָכוֹף אֶת יִצְרוֹ עָדִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the אוהב and שונא ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed nothing could outweigh animal pain. But overcoming your evil inclination is a stronger reason to choose the enemy.

steps.title: Proof from the rule that 'enemy' means only a Jewish enemy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the 'enemy' that the rule speaks about is a Jewish enemy and not a gentile one. If צער בעלי חיים were a Torah law, the owner's identity should not matter, so this seems to prove it is not a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The enemy they spoke about is a Jewish enemy, not a gentile enemy. If you say animal pain is a Torah law, why should it matter whether the enemy is Jewish or a gentile?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal suffers the same no matter who owns it. If the Torah required us to prevent animal pain, we would have to help the gentile's animal too. Since the ברייתא limits the rule to a Jewish enemy, it looks like animal pain is not the Torah's concern.

keyTerms.meaning: An enemy, someone you hate
The nations of the world, meaning gentiles
From the Torah, a Torah-level law
What difference does it make to me?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The enemy that they spoke about
is a Jewish enemy
and not a gentile enemy.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: If you say that animal pain is a Torah law,
what difference is it to me whether it is a Jewish enemy
or a gentile enemy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth source hinted at by the סימן in step 9 (שונא), a new attempt to show צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law.
steps.raayaObject: That צער בעלי חיים is not a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that limits 'enemy' to a Jewish enemy, excluding a gentile enemy

steps.title: The 'enemy' refers to the earlier ברייתא, not the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא's 'enemy' does not refer to the enemy in the פסוק about unloading. It refers to the enemy in the earlier ברייתא, where you help the enemy first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think the ברייתא is talking about the enemy in the פסוק? It is talking about the enemy in the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by explaining which 'enemy' the ברייתא meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'only a Jewish enemy' is not about which animal you must unload. It belongs to the earlier ברייתא (step 24), where you help the enemy first to break your יצר הרע. That reason applies to a Jewish enemy, so the limit says nothing about animal pain.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think...? (a way of showing the question is based on a wrong assumption)
The פסוק, the verse in the Torah
Refers to, is standing on
Here it means the ברייתא already quoted

steps.confusionAlert: Here מתניתין does not mean the משנה on our daf. It means the ברייתא from step 24 about the friend unloading and the enemy loading.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'Jewish enemy only' rule is about the earlier ברייתא, where helping the enemy comes first. It does not prove that animal pain is only a דרבנן concern.

phrases.english: Do you think it refers to the enemy of the verse?
phrases.notes: The פסוק is שמות 23:5, about the donkey of someone who hates you.

phrases.english: It refers to the enemy of the ברייתא.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from step 24: a friend needs unloading, an enemy needs loading, and you help the enemy first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 26 by changing which 'enemy' the ברייתא refers to.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully removes the proof. It does not prove the opposite side, though.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the 'enemy' was the one in the unloading פסוק. In fact it is the enemy from the earlier ברייתא about breaking one's יצר הרע.

steps.title: Opening another proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'come and hear' to start yet another proof about צער בעלי חיים. The source itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to bring another source to test whether צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proofs in the series have all been pushed off. The words תא שמע tell us the fifth source from the סימן in step 9 (רבצן) is about to be quoted on the same question.

keyTerms.meaning: Pain caused to animals; the question is whether preventing it is a Torah law

phrases.english: Come and hear:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 26 was rejected, the גמרא begins a new attempt.
steps.raayaObject: Whether צער בעלי חיים is a Torah law (the source is quoted next)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source that has not been quoted yet; it comes on the next amud
